items.text: The first three-way US–Russia–Ukraine talks since February opened in Abu Dhabi for two days, with [[p:Jared Kushner]] and [[p:Steve Witkoff]] mediating and security guarantees on the agenda. Kushner called it an initial step to build momentum; no European delegation is reported at the table. Russia's team under [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]] includes GRU chief [[p:Igor Kostyukov]] and deputy foreign minister [[p:Sergei Ryabkov]].
items.notes: French FM Barrot said on 8 Nov that Europeans would take part; AP reports no European delegation. Watch item W-261025-04.

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] hosted Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, at the White House to discuss Iran and afterwards cited "positive momentum", saying the US is "locked and loaded" but new strikes are "quite unlikely". [[p:Marco Rubio]] called Iran's demands outrageous and said no breakthrough is near. Tehran says it can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington ends the war on all fronts, unfreezes assets, lifts oil sanctions and ends its blockade. Brent fell to about $91.6.
items.outlet: Al Jazeera; AFP (via Arab News); Gulf News
items.notes: No agreement or next steps announced after the meeting. Gulf News outlines the Qatari-backed draft: day 1 US lifts blockade and releases some frozen funds; day 2 Hormuz reopens, then nuclear talks on highly enriched uranium. Rezaei on X accused the US of 'imaginary talks'.

items.text: US forces disabled the cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov, saying it tried to breach the blockade. Iranian local officials claim US strikes hit Qeshm Island on the night of 8 Nov; Rubio did not confirm them. The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] warned of a "devastating" response to any new attack.
items.outlet: Al Jazeera; Gulf News; Times of Israel
items.notes: Ship disabling reported by US side; Qeshm strikes are an Iranian claim only (state media reported explosions, cause unconfirmed). UAE National Guard rescued 22 crew from a burning ship (Gulf News).

items.text: [[p:Ahmed al-Sharaa]] and [[p:Mohammed bin Salman]] oversaw the signing of a Syrian–Saudi defence cooperation deal in Riyadh, alongside six Saudi loans worth $403m for health, housing, civil defence, power and water. Terms of the defence deal were not disclosed; Syria is weighing joining the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]].
items.notes: Sharaa's second Riyadh visit in under a month.

items.text: Yemeni military and government sources told AFP that up to 3,000 Syrian troops are deploying to Saudi Arabia and Yemen against the [[p:Houthis]], with hundreds already on both sides of the border and up to 10,000 possible later. Syria's state agency SANA quoted a source saying Damascus had not sent troops to Yemen "at this time" and that the deal focuses on training.
items.notes: Sources conflict: Yemeni sources vs SANA denial. Treat numbers as unconfirmed.

items.text: Turkey's [[p:Grand National Assembly of Turkey|parliament]] ratified the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]] by 279 votes to 119, completing ratification by all three members. Defence Minister [[p:Yaşar Güler]] said support for Saudi Arabia would be set later and aims at deterrence, and that Turkey does not foresee fighting the Houthis. The [[p:Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party|DEM Party]] and the Yeni Party voted against.
items.notes: No separate deployment motion reported yet; Al-Monitor expects training, advice and equipment rather than a large contingent.

items.text: Houthi missile and drone fire on Saudi Arabia continued: the coalition says it intercepted one drone and five missiles on 8 Nov and more over Riyadh on 9 Nov, and the East–West pipeline was attacked without disrupting operations. Yemen's government claims advances in western Lahj and east of al-Hazm in al-Jawf; the Houthis say Saudi jets carried out over 100 strikes in 24 hours. Neither side's claims are independently verified.
items.notes: Taiz under Houthi siege for over a month. Etihad cancelled Abu Dhabi–Riyadh/Dammam flights to 19 Nov.

items.text: Israel's 26th [[p:Knesset]] is sworn in today. [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] said he is open to [[p:Likud]] and [[p:Bezalel Smotrich]]'s party joining a government under him; [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] answered on 9 Nov by proposing a unity government under his own leadership. Eisenkot and [[p:Avigdor Lieberman]] agreed the next Speaker will come from Eisenkot's Yashar party, replacing Amir Ohana, but Lieberman rules out a minority government relying on Arab-led parties. [[p:United Torah Judaism]] is in contacts with the bloc; [[p:Shas]] says it stays with Netanyahu.
items.notes: Hebrew source, translated. Eisenkot's bloc 48 seats; with UTJ and Shas he would reach exactly 61. UTJ's key demand: a draft law shielded from High Court review (ynet).

items.text: Trump said part of the Republicans' midterm losses came from a "great dislike" of Israel, after [[p:JD Vance]] suggested the party may need to change its relationship with Israel. Trump said he had no problem with Vance linking the Iran war to the losses but still called the war one of the best things the US has done.
items.notes: Trump also said Eisenkot's and Netanyahu's policies are very similar.

items.text: The army ended its roughly ten-day Hebron operation on 2 Nov, launched after the 23 Oct checkpoint attack that killed two soldiers; Hebron's municipality says more than 3,000 people were displaced, and the attackers' homes were demolished. [[p:Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs|OCHA]] recorded 457 settler attacks causing casualties or damage in October, the most in any month since it began counting in 2006. On 4 Nov about 30 settlers took over eight Palestinian homes near Jericho.
items.notes: Jericho takeover at Ein al-Duyuk al-Tahta; Haaretz says Central Command chief knew in advance, which the army denies. 377 olive-harvest attacks since 1 Sept (OCHA).

items.text: The first big storm of the season flooded about 70,000 tents in 12 hours and killed at least five people, according to Gaza's Government Media Office, which says Israel is admitting only 20,000 of 200,000 tents. The health ministry counts 20 killed by Israeli fire in the past week and 1,613 since the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel told the UN on 1 Nov it would suspend shipments from Egypt; the [[p:Board of Peace]] urged Israel to let winter supplies in.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Casualty and shelter figures from Gaza authorities, not independently verified. No ISF deployment reported.

items.text: Israeli artillery and air strikes hit al-Mansouri, Majdal Zoun, al-Qantara and Kfar Tebnit in the south on 9 Nov. Prime Minister [[p:Nawaf Salam]] told the cabinet Lebanon's priority is to stay out of a new war. Many Lebanese are stockpiling and packing go-bags, fearing renewed US or Israeli strikes on Iran could pull [[p:Hezbollah]] back in.
items.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation
items.notes: Arabic source, translated. Health ministry toll since 2 Mar: 4,390 killed, 12,429 wounded. Salhani piece (6 Nov) is reporting plus analysts' views.

items.text: Foreign Minister [[p:Fuad Hussein]] said the US Treasury asked Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except two, which he called hard to do without hurting the economy. He said Iraq reached an understanding with Washington to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman and put war losses at $60bn. Iraq reopens the Sheeb crossing on 10 Nov and temporarily closes Mandali from 13 Nov.
items.outlet: Reuters (via Arab News); Khaleej Times (citing INA)
items.notes: Iraqi exports rose to about 3.5m bpd in October.

items.text: Iran's judiciary said three men arrested in the January protests in Karaj were executed after the Supreme Court upheld their sentences. [[p:Iran Human Rights]] counts at least 81 executions on political charges from January to October, including 32 protesters.
items.notes: Iran International is a London-based opposition-leaning outlet; the executions were announced by the judiciary. Names not given.

items.text: [[p:Rafael Grossi]] told the UN Security Council that Iran must give the [[p:IAEA|International Atomic Energy Agency]] immediate access to verify its nuclear material, in the first IAEA referral of Iran to the Council over reporting obligations in 20 years. Iran's envoy accused the Council of double standards over the US–Israeli strikes; no vote was held.
items.notes: IAEA says 440.9 kg of 60% uranium unaccounted for. China, Russia and Niger voted against the board referral. Watch W-261027-04.

items.text: Syria reopened the Nasib crossing with Jordan on 28 Oct and the two agreed a joint security committee to investigate Jordan's strikes after the Karak church attack. Two days later Jordanian guards repelled about 14 gunmen crossing from Syria, wounding several.
items.notes: Syria says Jordan's strikes killed seven civilians; Jordan says two ISIS members.

items.text: France blamed a unit of Iran's [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] for the October cyberattack that shut down refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets, summoned Iran's ambassador and said it will seek EU sanctions. Foreign Minister [[p:Jean-Noël Barrot]] said France rules nothing out in its response; Paris prosecutors opened an investigation.
items.notes: French pages could not be opened in full; details from SBS summary and French headlines (franceinfo, Ouest-France).

items.text: [[p:Vladimir Putin]] met [[p:Masoud Pezeshkian]] at the gas exporters' summit in Moscow; Putin cited 10.4% trade growth and continued work at Bushehr, and Pezeshkian said the region does not need US help.

Two trains collided at al-Ayyat in Giza, killing seven and injuring over 110; MPs are pressing the transport minister to resign. Separately, [[p:Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] ordered a new emergency agency to build strategic reserves.
Human Rights Watch filed a third-party intervention as the European Court of Human Rights prepares to rule on the detention of Istanbul mayor [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]].
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
